security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's TCG implementation of HLV*/HSV* performs memory tag checks without first consulting hstatus.MTAG_I (which should suppress checks when set) and without checking VS-stage leaf PTE.X (which also forces unchecked loads), causing tag faults or unchecked accesses at times the spec forbids
security_spec.summary: HLV/HSV tag-check opt-out via hstatus.MTAG_I and VS-stage PTE.X: if QEMU TCG helper_hyp_load/store does not suppress MTE tag checks when hstatus.MTAG_I==1 or VS-stage leaf PTE.X==1, the hypervisor experiences spurious tag faults on code-page accesses, allowing a malicious guest to construct page tables where hypervisor-emulated loads diverge from guest-native loads and bypass memory tagging enforcement

findings.finding: check_access_hlsv() sets mmu_idx for HLV/HSV helpers. No MTE/MemTag infrastructure exists for RISC-V in this QEMU (no hstatus.MTAG_I bit, no PTE.MTAG bit, no tag-check logic). The function correctly computes privilege mode and two-stage translation attributes for the HLV/HSV access path. There is nothing to opt out of because MTE is not implemented.
No HSTATUS_MTAG_I or HSTATUS_MTAG bit is defined. The hstatus register lacks any MTE/MemTag control field. Without this bit, no HLV/HSV tag suppression can occur — neither correctly nor incorrectly.
No PTE.MTAG bit is defined in the PTE bit layout. The page table entry format has no memory-tagging field, so the VS-stage leaf PTE.X override path described in the security spec cannot exist.

All HLV/HSV helper functions (hlv_bu, hlv_hu, hlv_wu, hlv_d, hsv_b, hsv_h, hsv_w, hsv_d) perform standard cpu_ld*_mmu / cpu_st*_mmu accesses through check_access_hlsv(). No MTE tag check logic exists to incorrectly trigger tag faults or incorrectly suppress them.

riscv_cpu_tlb_fill() handles TLB fills for HLV/HSV accesses via the two-stage lookup path. Contains no MTE/MemTag logic — no tag checks, no hstatus.MTAG_I consultation. Since MTE is not implemented for RISC-V, this is the correct baseline behavior.

get_physical_address() performs the page-table walk for address translation. Contains no MTE/MemTag logic. The PTE bit checks handle R/W/X/A/D/U/G/PBMT/N but not MTAG. No tag-check or tag-suppression logic is present, which is correct since the feature is unimplemented.
